subject: Aegis: Jun 5 peak — latency/errors impact / follow-through & owner commitments
messages:
From: Cecilia Ramos <cecilia.ramos@aegis.ai>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai
Cc: SRE Lead <sre-lead@aegis.ai>
Date: 2027-06-06 09:12 -0700
Subject: Severe latency & elevated errors during Jun 5 peak

Hi Michael,

We observed a significant service degradation on Jun 5 between 14:03 and 14:48 UTC that impacted our customer-facing chat (approx. 27% of sessions). Symptoms: sustained latency spikes (~3-5s per response vs baseline 400-600ms), spike in 5xx error rate (~7% of requests), and a throughput drop of ~60% on the Redwood hosted endpoint. This coincided with our regional spike (US-WEST) and affected our premium customers.

We attached a short timeline and a few request IDs / sample traces for your SREs. We need an exec-level readout and a clear remediation plan with owners — Aegis leadership is requesting:
- Immediate mitigations we can rely on in the next 48 hours
- RCA and corrective-action commit timeline (owners + dates)
- Any temporary SLA/credit proposals while you remediate

This is blocking our weekend rollout unless we have commitments. Please loop in engineering and CS leads.

Attachments: aegis-incident-timeline.csv (timeline + sample traces)

Thanks,
Cecilia Ramos
VP, Ops — Aegis AI
From: michael.grant@redwood.ai
To: Cecilia Ramos <cecilia.ramos@aegis.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-06 09:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe latency & elevated errors during Jun 5 peak

Cecilia — thanks for the heads-up and the traces. I’m really sorry for the disruption. We’re treating this as highest priority. Immediate notes:

1) Triage & mitigations (in flight):
   - Routing: temporarily routing Aegis traffic to a dedicated GPU pool in us-west (reduces cold-start and tail latency exposure) — will apply within 30m.
   - Fallback: enabling a faster quantized model variant as a fallback for interactive paths to keep p99 latency lower.
   - Autoscaling: forcing a higher reserve cap for your org while we complete post-incident fixes.

2) Next steps:
   - I’ll convene a short readout with our SRE, product, and account team today within 2 hours.
   - We’ll produce a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with owners and dates within 72 hours and a preliminary RCA within 48 hours.

I’ve looped in our SRE lead (Priyom) and Customer Success (Kimberly, Monica) to own technical and account follow-through respectively. Priyom — please post an initial remediation checklist (what we’re changing now + logs we need) and owner assignments.

I’ve attached the initial mitigation snippets we’re pushing to the control plane so you can see what we’ll change.

[Attachment: initial-mitigation-snippets.txt]

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-06 10:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe latency & elevated errors during Jun 5 peak — SRE actions

Michael / all — quick SRE update and owners (internal):

Root cause hypothesis (working): increased burst of long-context requests triggered uneven KV cache pressure + a suboptimal kernel choice for that specific seq_len distribution on our default runtime image. That combination caused queueing and some request timeouts under load.

Immediate actions (now — owners):
 - Priyom (me): force-route Aegis to dedicated pool; enable aggressive async batching threshold to reduce per-token overhead — ETA 30m (in flight).
 - Neha Kapoor: flip to quantized fallback variant on chat route (keeps p95 low), ETA 45m.
 - Monica Patel: pause non-essential background jobs from that tenant (eg. large-batch embeddings), ETA 20m.
 - Kimberly Park: prepare customer comms and the MAP template, collate affected customers list, ETA 60m.

Follow-up (24–72h):
 - Deep kernel profile & telemetry correlation (Priyom + infra) — publish RCA draft within 48h.
 - Runtime patch: kernel selection logic fix and a small scheduler change — target canary by EOD+1 and rollout in 72h.

Artifacts we need from Aegis (Cecilia):
 - Confirm sample trace IDs in aegis-incident-timeline.csv are representative (Cecilia, please confirm).
 - Traffic pattern during the window (burst distribution by session length).

I’ll update the MAP doc with the owner table right after the immediate mitigations land.

— Priyom
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: michael.grant@redwood.ai
To: Cecilia Ramos <cecilia.ramos@aegis.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-06 12:10 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan (draft) & exec readout time — Aegis Jun 5 incident

Cecilia — attaching the MAP draft and a short owner/timeline table. Proposed readout window: today 16:00 PST / 23:00 UTC (30 min) with execs on both sides (you suggested that cadence). Agenda: timeline, immediate mitigations landed, RCA hypothesis, 72h plan + SLA/credit proposal.

Key commitments (excerpt):
- 6/6 (same day): mitigations deployed (routing + quantized fallback) — Owner: Priyom
- 6/7: Canary runtime kernel fix and scheduler patch — Owner: Infra Eng (Prio team)
- 6/9: Full rollout + post-rollout validation + monitoring knobs — Owner: Neha
- 6/10: Final RCA document + exec summary — Owner: Michael / Priyom

We’ve also prepared a provisional service credit proposal (10% for the impacted window) and a temporary SLA increase for your org while we stabilize. We’ll finalize after the RCA.

[Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx]

Link to MAP (read only): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AegisMAP
HubSpot record: HS-AEG-3221

Please confirm the readout time and whether Procurement should join.

Best,
Michael
From: Cecilia Ramos <cecilia.ramos@aegis.ai>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai
Cc: SRE Lead <sre-lead@aegis.ai>, Procurement <procurement@aegis.ai>
Date: 2027-06-06 12:39 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan (draft) & exec readout time — Aegis Jun 5 incident

Thanks — 16:00 PST works. We appreciate the quick mitigations; our SREs saw a drop in p95 after routing changes. A few asks to capture on the call:
- We’d like a firm timeline for the kernel selection patch and a canary plan (including rollback triggers).
- We’ll need a formal credit proposal for review (Procurement is looped).
- Executive attendance: our CTO will join for 10 minutes for the readout.

We’ll review the MAP and send any edits prior to the readout.

Cecilia
VP, Ops — Aegis AI
From: michael.grant@redwood.ai
To: Cecilia Ramos <cecilia.ramos@aegis.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-10 17:45 -0700
Subject: Final RCA & commitments — Aegis Jun 5 incident

Cecilia — thanks again for the readout and the collaborative MAP review. Per follow-through: attached is our Final RCA (concise exec summary + technical appendix) and the closure table with owners and dates. Executive summary (brief):

- Root cause: a combination of (1) an unexpected long-tail shift in session context lengths that increased KV cache churn and (2) a kernel selection heuristic that mis-ranked a slower path under that distribution. The interaction caused queue buildup and increased timeouts.

Corrective actions and status:
- Runtime kernel selection fix: patched and canaried 6/8 — full rollout completed 6/9. Owner: Infra Eng (Priyom) — STATUS: Complete
- Scheduler tweak to limit per-tenant queueing under burst windows: deployed 6/7 — STATUS: Complete
- MAP post-deploy validation: automated checks added to per-tenant dashboards — STATUS: Complete
- Documentation & guardrails: new guidance published for on-call and account teams — STATUS: Complete

Service credit & SLA: we’re offering a 10% credit for the impacted billing window and a temporary SLA guarantee (99.9% p95 target for your account) while we monitor for the next 30 days. Procurement, I’ve included the credit proposal in the MAP and am happy to take next steps.

Attachments: final-rca.pdf (exec + appendix), aegis-incident-timeline.csv (revised)

Ask: please confirm acceptance of the MAP and the credit proposal by EOD 6/14 so we can close the loop and move to operational monitoring.

— Michael Grant
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
